solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ada, rusty, exercising for twenty-four period

indicators.note: exercising works the body into new positions, so these letters get moved about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ada, stiff and out of practice, spends a full day working out.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas make Ada and rusty look like a person and her condition; they are simply the letters to rearrange into SATURDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday is one particular day of the week, and a day lasts twenty-four hours, so it is a named example.

clue.text: German villain holds something for forging

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A German baddie is in possession of some forgery kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Forging suggests faking documents, as a villain might; here it is the blacksmith's craft of hammering hot metal on an ANVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith shapes heated iron by hammering it on this heavy iron block, the central piece of smithing equipment.

clue.text: United sailors in vessel

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United, as in football club names
RN is the Royal Navy, whose members are sailors

explanation.surface: A combined crew of sailors aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessel suggests a ship, which fits the sailors, but it is the other sense: a container such as a large vase.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel can be any container for liquid or ashes, and an urn is a tall rounded example of one.

clue.text: Complexity of small section attached to hospital

blocks.note: DEPT is the short form of department, a section of an organisation, with small signalling the abbreviation
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: The complicated structure of a small hospital unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Small here tells you to shorten department, the usual reading of section in an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth in thought or a subject means profundity or intricacy, much the same as complexity.

clue.text: Messing around idly, Dee gave up

indicators.note: messing around means fooling about without order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After lazily fooling about, Dee eventually surrendered.
explanation.walkthrough: Idly reads as an adverb describing how Dee messed around, but it is part of the letters to rearrange with Dee.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender or concede, which is exactly what giving up means in a contest or argument.

clue.text: Leading Roman Catholic staying in a hotel

indicators.note: a guest staying in a building is inside it, so one piece is placed within the others

blocks.note: taken as written
RC is the standard abbreviation for Roman Catholic
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A senior Catholic cleric is booked into a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: Leading Roman Catholic reads as a bishop or cardinal, but leading stands alone as the definition, as in arch-rival or archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective or prefix, arch means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy, so it matches leading.

clue.text: An hour after midday, people with time for reconcilliation

blocks.note: one o'clock in the afternoon, as the phrase 'at one'
men are people
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Meeting people at lunchtime to make peace after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: One o'clock is read as a time phrase rather than a number; note that the clue misspells reconciliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement originally meant being at one with someone, the restoring of harmony between estranged parties, hence making amends.

clue.text: Sat on beam, fence – regularly picked up sticks

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
in a down entry, picking something up lifts it, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Someone perched on a beam of a fence and gathered twigs.
explanation.walkthrough: Picked up sticks paints someone collecting kindling; sticks is really a verb meaning glues, and picked up works on the letters instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement is a binding agent, so to cement things is to bond or glue them together, as sticks does.

clue.text: Cooker of very exquisite nosh (starters only)

indicators.note: starters are the openings of a meal, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A cook who turns out superb food, as long as it is only the starters.
explanation.walkthrough: Starters fits the food theme as a first course; nosh is British slang for food. The word 'of' belongs to the letters, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is the enclosed heated compartment of a stove, the part of a kitchen range used for baking and roasting.

clue.text: Quietly changes shapes in advance

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly
to reform is to change something, usually for the better

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly alters things before anyone notices.
explanation.walkthrough: Shapes looks like a noun, but it is a verb, matching the verb form of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Preforming something means moulding or forming it beforehand, before its final use, so it is shaping ahead of time.

clue.text: Turned white with pain, having spilled blood all around

indicators.note: something all around another encloses it on every side, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to have spilled blood is to have bled
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Someone went pale in agony after losing blood everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Turned white reads as going pale from pain, but it is the definition of whitened by chemicals or sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleaching removes colour, so something bleached has been made white or much paler, typically by chemicals or sunlight.

clue.text: Trams made to crash in European capital

indicators.note: a crash smashes things into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone forced trams to collide in a European capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Made reads as part of 'made to crash', but it is part of the letters with trams.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital city of the Netherlands, one example of a European capital.

clue.text: From what we hear, deserve to get the bird

indicators.note: what we hear is sound rather than spelling, so the word is judged by how it is spoken

blocks.note: to earn something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: Apparently you deserve to be booed off, getting the bird being British slang for being jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, to get the bird is to be hissed or jeered at, which fits deserve; here the bird is literal, a sea eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a large bird that crosswords use constantly because of its handy letters.

clue.text: Tool found in workbench is electric

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the ends and starts of three words

explanation.surface: A power tool is kept at a workbench.
explanation.walkthrough: Electric suggests a power tool you might look for, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chisel is a bladed hand implement for cutting or shaping wood and stone, one example of a tool.

clue.text: Bull and pig clean

blocks.note: a hog is a pig
to wash is to clean

explanation.surface: A farmyard scene of a bull and a pig being scrubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bull looks like another farm animal next to pig, but it is slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull is short for a coarse slang word for rubbish talk, and hogwash is likewise nonsense or empty claims.

clue.text: Book by unknown author following the French state

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so the order of the pieces is set

blocks.note: le is a French word for the
B is the abbreviation for book
anon, short for anonymous, is written for an author whose name is unknown

explanation.surface: An anonymous book about the French state.
explanation.walkthrough: The French state looks like the definition, meaning France; the definition is only state, and the French gives the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is an independent country on the eastern Mediterranean, one example of a sovereign state or nation.

clue.text: Stylish Tessa coming out of her shell, outwardly dull

indicators.note: a shell is the outer casing, so losing it strips away the outside letters and keeps the middle
something outwardly on the surface surrounds what is within, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: something dry is dull and uninteresting
the name without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Shy Tessa is finally blossoming, becoming fashionable though still rather boring on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: Coming out of her shell is the idiom for a shy person growing confident; here it removes the name's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy describes clothes or a person that are smart and elegant, the fashionable look that stylish describes.

clue.text: Fit to dispute losing right

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: to argue is to dispute
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone well-placed to argue a case they lose, forfeiting their right.
explanation.walkthrough: Fit reads as an adjective meaning suitable, but it is a noun: a bout of shivering fever.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a malarial fever marked by attacks of shivering, so it is a fit or paroxysm of illness.

clue.text: Seb, taken aback by over-the-top editor, becoming obsessed

indicators.note: taken aback suggests something pulled backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the name as written
OTT is the usual abbreviation for over-the-top
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Seb is startled by an extravagant editor who is turning fixated on something.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken aback means startled in the surface; in the wordplay it turns the name around.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone besotted is infatuated, so fixated on a person that they can think of nothing else, which is to be obsessed.

clue.text: One eating no fat fish

blocks.note: first meaning: Jack of the nursery rhyme, who could eat no fat
second meaning: a small herring-like sea fish

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning comes from the nursery rhyme 'Jack Sprat could eat no fat, his wife could eat no lean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack in the rhyme refuses fatty food, and the same name is a small silvery food fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Lie around in the morning after returning message

indicators.note: to be around something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the other
to return is to go back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Someone lounges about in the morning after coming home, then sends a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Lie around reads as lazing about; the wrapping happens first and then the whole lot is turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic letter sent over the internet, one kind of message or communication.

clue.text: Horticulturist’s fantastic red range

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and unreal, so these letters take on an invented form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant grower boasts a wonderful selection of red blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s reads as possession but stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A horticulturist cultivates plants, and a gardener is the everyday word for someone who tends plants and flowers.

clue.text: Article in study for head of college

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a den is a private room for study or work
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece written in a private room for the college principal.
explanation.walkthrough: Article reads as a written piece but is the grammatical article, and study is the room, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: At many universities and Oxbridge colleges the head of a faculty or college, or a senior officer, holds the title dean.

clue.text: Note exclamation of annoyance

blocks.note: first meaning: the first note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt do
second meaning: the cry made famous by Homer Simpson

explanation.walkthrough: The sol-fa scale runs do, re, mi and so on; the first note is often spelt with an h in British crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the tonic in solmisation and is also the cry uttered on realising one's own stupid mistake.

clue.text: Say nothing? Am false!

blocks.note: sh is what you say to call for silence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they should stay silent, then confesses to being a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: Say nothing looks like advice to keep quiet; it gives the hushing sound.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, sham means fake or bogus, not genuine, which is what false means here.

clue.text: Crazy and terrible situation in which you’ll find Hazel?

blocks.note: nuts is slang for crazy
a hell is a dreadful place or situation

explanation.surface: A woman named Hazel finds herself in a mad, awful predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: Hazel looks like a woman's name, hence the capital; it is the hazelnut, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazelnut kernel sits inside a hard woody casing, so its situation or home is this shell.
